national_indicator_definition: The indicator presents government budget allocations for research and development (GBARD) for agriculture in Bosnia and Herzegovina. GBARD data measure public support for research and development activities and provide information on the extent of public funding for research and development in agriculture. Values are expressed in million euro at current prices.
national_rationale: The indicator provides information on the level of public funding for research and development directed towards agriculture. Monitoring allocations for research and development in this area provides information on investments that can support agricultural productivity, sustainable and resilient food production systems and food security.
national_methodology_characteristics: Data for the indicator in Bosnia and Herzegovina are based on government budget allocations for research and development (GBARD) for the socio-economic objective of agriculture. The data are collected and compiled within research and development statistics in accordance with international methodological standards used for GBARD, including the guidelines of the OECD Frascati Manual 2015 and the European Business Statistics Methodological Manual for R&D statistics 2023. For international comparability, the indicator is presented within the Eurostat sdg_02_30 dataset. Data are expressed in million euro at current prices. When comparing data between countries, methodological differences should be taken into account, including the stage of the budgetary process from which the data are derived, namely whether they are based on final budget appropriations or actual outlays, as well as the treatment of VAT or EU funds for research and development. The data for Bosnia and Herzegovina published by the Agency for Statistics of Bosnia and Herzegovina represent the national data series for this indicator.
national_long_objective: No specific quantitative national target has been established for this indicator in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The indicator is monitored through changes over time in public funding allocated to research and development in agriculture, based on the available time series.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator refers to Government budget allocations for R&D (GBARD) for agriculture. GBARD data measure government support to research and development (R&D) activities, or, in other words, how much priority governments place on the public funding of R&D. GBARD data are compiled using the guidelines laid out in the OECD’s Frascati Manual from 2015 and and the European Business Statistics Methodological Manual for R&D statistics of 2023. The data are expressed in current prices, meaning that the overall development of the indicator is in part also influenced by general price inflation.
eu_rationale: Indicator is used to monitor progress towards SDG 2 on ending hunger and malnutrition; which are embedded in the European Commission’s 2024-2029 Priorities under 'Sustaining our quality of life: Food security, water and nature'.  SDG 2 - among other things - aims to ensure access to safe, nutritious and sufficient food. Improving agricultural productivity and maintaining sustainable and resilient food production systems are key factors in achieving this goal and depend to a large extend on increased investment in agricultural, food and nutrition research and development.
eu_methodology_characteristics:
Countries compile GBARD data following the Frascati manual recommendations. Among the few methodological issues which can affect the comparisons across countries, are the stage in the budgetary process from which final GBARD data are drawn (final budget appropriations or actual outlays); the inclusion of VAT or EU funds for R&D. GBARD data are broken down by:
  -Socio-economic objectives (SEOs) in accordance to the Nomenclature for the analysis and comparison of scientific programmes and budgets (NABS 2007). - (See Annex 3 at the bottom of the page).
  -Funding mode: project funding and institutional funding (non-mandatory data).
The part of GBARD allocated to transnational cooperation in R&D is further broken down into three specific categories: transnational public R&D performers; Europe-wide transnational public R&D programmes; and bilateral or multilateral public R&D programmes established between Member State governments or with EFTA and candidate countries.
eu_long_objective: The long-term objective by 2030 is the transition from basic institutional financing to systemic support for innovation and rural development, while increasing the allocation of public funds for agricultural research and development to a minimum of 2% to 3% of the total budget.
